annotation.title_clean: Council Directive of 25 July 1985 on the approximation of the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the Member States concerning liability for defective products (85/374/EEC)
annotation.title_en: Council Directive of 25 July 1985 on the approximation of the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the Member States concerning liability for defective products (85/374/EEC)
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Communities
annotation.summary_en: The 1985 EU Product Liability Directive establishes strict, no-fault producer liability for damage caused by defective movable products, harmonising Member State laws. It defines product, producer, defect, defences, damage, and limitation periods. It is the foundational liability framework later applied to robots and AI products, though it does not mention them.
key_provisions_or_claims: Producers are strictly liable for damage caused by a defect in their products (Art. 1).
A product is defective if it lacks the safety a person is entitled to expect (Art. 6).
Injured person must prove damage, defect and causation (Art. 4).
Defences include development risk and compliance with mandatory regulations (Art. 7).
Three-year limitation period and 10-year long-stop from market placement (Arts. 10-11).
